MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  DECEMBER 9, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting to order at 5:32 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Doug Stewart; Mayor Pro Tem Marianne Riggins;  and
  Councilmembers Paul Grisanti, Bruce Silverstein and Steve Uhring.

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Joseph Toney, Assistant City
  Manager; Alexis Brown, Deputy City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin
  Riesgo, Community Services Director; Yolanda Bundy, Environmental Sustainability
  Director; Maureen Tamuri, Interim Planning Director; Rob DuBouX, Public ‘Works
  Director; Parker Davis, Media Technician; Christina Munoz, Deputy City Clerk; Jasdn
  Lawrence, Deputy City Clerk; and Tracey Rossine, Environmental Programs Manager

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Edward Albrecht led the Pledge of Allegiance.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on
  November 27, 2024.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Uhring seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda and adj ourn in memory of P.J. Dahl and Kim Lamorie. The
  question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.
ITEM 1  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Mayor Stewart opened the floor to public comment. As there were no public
  speakers present for the Consent Calendar, the Mayor returned the matter to the
  table for discussion.

  Item Nos. l.B.4. and l.B.7. were pulled by the Council.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of December 9, 2024
  Page 2 0f 10

  MOTION  Councilmember Grisanti moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Riggins seconded a motion
  to approve the Consent Calendar, pulling Item Nos 1.B.4. and 1.B.7. The motion
  carried unanimously.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Waive Further Reading
  Recommended Action: After the City Attorney has read the title, waive full
  reading of ordinances considered on this agenda for introduction on first
  reading and/or second reading and adoption.
  2.  A_pprove Warrants
  Recommended Action: Allow and approve warrant demand numbers
  74300—74356 on the register from the General Fund and direct the City
  Manager to pay out the funds to each of the claimants listed in Warrant
  Register No. 759 in the amount of the warrant appearing opposite their
  names, for the purposes stated on the respective demands in a total amount
  of $2,906,897.75. City of Malibu payroll check number 5490-5492 and
  ACH deposits were issued in the amount of $384,93 1 .89.
  3.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the October 23, 2024
  Special Meeting, the October 724, 2024 Special Meeting, the October 28,
  2024 Regular Meeting.
  5.  Resolution Extending the Declaration of the Existence of a Local
  Emergencv Regarding Conditions on Pacific Coast Highway (PCH)
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 24-61 extending the
  declaration of the existence of a local emergency related to the increase of
  reckless and illegal driving on pacific coast highway and directing staff to
  coordinate efforts with other governmental agencies to increase attention
  and create programs to reduce the risk and danger associated with pacific
  coast highway in the City.
  6.  Resolution Extending the Declaration of the Existence of a Local
  Emergency and Continuing a Program for Reducing the Risk of Fires
  Associated with Individuals Engaged in Unpermitted Camping
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 24—62 extending the
  declaration of the existence of a local emergency and continuing a program
  for reducing the risk of fires associated with individuals engaged in
  unpermitted camping.

  The following items were pulled from the consent calendar for individual consideration:

  4.  Professional Services Agreements for Contract Flaming Services
  Recommended Action: 1) Authorize the Mayor to execute a professional
J  services agreement with Civic Solutions, Inc. for contract planning services;
  and 2) Authorize the Mayor to execute a professional services agreement
  with Rincon Consultants, Inc. for contract planning services.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of Decembar 9, 2024
  Page 3 0f 10

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

  MOTION  Councilmember Uhring moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Riggins seconded a
  motion to: l) authorize the Mayor to execute a professional services
  agreement with Civic Solutions, Inc. for contract planning services; and 2)
  authorize the Mayor to execute a professional services agreement with
  Rincon Consultants, Inc. for contract planning services. The motion carried
  unanimously.

  7.  November 5. 2024 General Municipal Election Results
  Recommended Action: Adopt Resolution No. 24-63 reciting the facts of
  the General Municipal Election held on November 5, 2024 and declaring
  the result and such other matters as provided by law.

  City Clerk Pettij ohn presented the staff report.

  MOTION  Councilmember Silverstein moved, and Mayor Pro Tem Riggins seconded
  a motion to adopt Resolution No. 24—63 reciting the facts of the General
  Municipal Election held on November 5, 2024 and declaring the result and
  such other matters as provided by law. The motion carried unanimously.
t  ITEM 2  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  City Council Reorganization

  l.  Presentations to Outgoing Councilmember

  The following individuals made presentations to Councilmember Grisanti:

  Councilmember Edward Albrecht (City of Calabasas), Nick Fariessm (State
  Senator Ben Allen), Anthony Avila (Assemblymember Irwin), Sergeant
  Chris Soderlund (Los Angeles County Sheriffs Department), Shari Davis
  (Santa Monica College), Sohpia Soudani (Supervisor Horvath), and Terry
  Dipple (Las Virgenes-Malibu Council of Governments)

  Mayor Stewart made presentations on behalf of the City of Agoura Hills,
  City of Hidden Hills, City of Westlake Village, and City of Malibu.

  2.  Remarks by Outgoing Councilmember

  Councilmember Grisanti thanked the residents, city staff, his appointed
  commissioners, and Sheriff’s Department staff. He discussed his plans to
  continue serving the Malibu community, including working with Smart
~m mpw
  .__J  Coast California and Pepperdine University. He thanked Mayor Pro Tem
  Riggins and Mayor Stewart for working with him on Ad Hoc Committees.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of December 9, 2024
  Page 4 of 10

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins and Mayor Stewart thanked Councilmember
  Grisanti for his service.

  3.  Adj ournment of 17th City Council

  At 6:06 p.1n., Mayor Stewart adjourned the 17m City Council.

  4.  Reconvene 18th City Council

  Mayor Stewart called the meeting of the 18th City Council to order at 6:06
  pm.
  5.  Administration of Oath of Office to Newly Elected Councilmembers

  Bruce Silverstein was sworn in by Louis Silverstein.

  Steve Uhring was sworn in by Marcia Rybak.

  Haylynn Conrad was sworn in by Ell Conrad.

  6.  Remarks by Newly Elected Councilmembers

  Councilmember Silverstein congratulated Councilmember Uhring and-
  Councilmember Conrad and discussed the election results and historic
  election results. He thanked his family, residents who supported his
  campaign, and The Malibu Times publisher Hayley Mattson. He discussed
  the history and spirit of Malibu. He discussed changes in Malibu that were
  not compatible with the Vision Statement and Mission Statement and the
  various factors contributing to those changes. He discussed his 2020
  campaign and his service on the City Council. He discussed his goals to
  serve the Malibu community.

  Councilmember Uhring congratulated Councilmember Silverstein and
  Councilmember Conrad. He thanked the Pepperdine University journalism
  students for covering the election. He thanked his wife and the voters who
  re—elected him.

  Councilmember Conrad thanked her husband and her kids, her family, her
  friends, and residents who supported her campaign. She discussed the
  unique environment and spirit of Malibu. She discussed her commitment
  to improving safety in Malibu and preserving the rural nature of the City.
  She discussed the importance of cultivating an environment oftransparency
  and civility. She thanked the public for the opportunity to serve.
Fm“,
  ITEM 3  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of December 9, 2024
  Page 5 of 10

  Josh Spiegel, Public Safety Commission, provided an update on license plate
  readers. He discussed the increased success rate for the homeless outreach team in
  getting people housed. He commended LAZ Parking for their work on parking
  enforcement for the City. He discussed the importance of installing a radio repeater
  at Bluff” s Park for emergency radio alerts and discussed delays due to the Flaming
  process. He proposed deploying satellite internet systems during Public Safety
  Power Shutoff events.

  Mayor Stewart discussed the rules of decorum and requested the public hold thei
  applause.

  Assistant City Manager Toney discussed the Particularly Dangerous Situation Red
  Flag Warning scheduled through Wednesday evening. He stated a Public Safety
  Power Shutoff (PSPS) was in effect and several circuits were being powered down,
  including City Hall’s circuit. He stated the Fire Department had augmented staffing
  through the wind event and the Sheriff’s Department was on alert as well. He
  announced Trancas Park and Charmlee Wilderness Park were closed due to the
  wind event and emergency generators were ready to be deployed at intersections in
  case of evacuation. He stated PSPS information was available on the City’s
  website. He stated the City was prepared to activate the Emergency Operations
  Center if needed. He announced the City’s Housing Element had been certified by
  the California Department of Housing and Community Development. He stated
  staff would be providing regular updates regarding the Community Lands project
  at future meetings. He provided an update on the PCH Signal Synchronization
  Project construction. He stated the speed cameras on PCH should be operational
  by the end of 2025. He discussed plans for temporary roundabouts on PCH at El
  Matador and Encinal Canyon Road. He announced the next PCH Master Plan
  workshop on December 11, 2025. He announced that the City Council would be
  dark for the second meeting in December and City Hall would be closed December
  24, 2024-January l, 2025 for a family-friendly winter holiday closure.

  Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, announced
  there were 33 part one crimes in November and the yearly average was down from
  the year before. He discussed an incident where a Sheriffs Department vehicle
  was rearended on PCH. He discussed an incident where deputies responded to
  shots fired near Carbon Mesa. He stated there were no injuries and the suspect was
  apprehended.

ITEM 4.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Tim Pera, Mountains Recreation Conservation Authority (MRCA) Ranger,
  welcomed Councilmember Conrad. He presented the monthly ranger report. He
  reported 203 parking citations were issued and continuous overnight patrols were
  scheduled for red flag events. He stated there were increased ranger patrols at
  Escondido Park due to increased traffic. He stated three administrative citations
  were issued for dogs on the beach and possession of alcohol at Lechuza Beach. He
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of December 9, 2024
  Page 6 of 10

discussed maintenance work near Big Rock Drive.

Channing Frykman discussed the campaign experience and thanked City Clerk
Pettij ohn, the Department Heads, and staff. She thanked Councilmember Grisanti
for his service and congratulated Councilmember Silverstein, Councilmember
Uhring, and Councilmember Conrad on their election.

Scott Dittrich congratulated Councilmember Silverstein, Councilmember Uhring,
and Councilmember Conrad on their election and discussed Councilmember
Grisanti’s service to the community. He discussed PSPS events and how they
impacted the community. He discussed short-term rental regulations and the
Coastal Commission. He discussed fire fuel levels and the danger.

Sue Murphree congratulated Councilmember Silverstein, Councilmember Uhring,
and Councilmember Conrad. She requested the Malibu Marlins and Malibu
Aquatics Club swim programs share the pool and discussed low enrollment in the
Malibu Marlins for Winter.

Colin Drummond congratulated Councilmember Silverstein, Councilmember
Uhring, and Councilmember Conrad on their election. He indicated support for
Ms. Murphree’s comments and requested the programs be allowed to share the
pool. He suggested increasing the number ofkids allowed per lane to make it easier
to share the pool.

Jo Drummond congratulated Councilmember Silverstein, Councilmember Uhring,
Councilmember Conrad on their election. She requested members of the public
that participate in hybrid meetings sign up in advance and be shown on camera.
She discussed the history ofthe Malibu Aquatics Club Malibu Seawolves team and
indicated support for the two swim programs sharing the pool.

Kim Ford, former co-president for Malibu Seawolves, discussed the challenge of
commuting for a swim program and requested pool time in Malibu.

Norm Haynie congratulated Councilmember Silverstein, Councilmember Uhring,
and Councilmember Conrad on their election, and commended all Councilmembers
for their service. He thanked Councilmember Grisanti for his service.

Patrick Murphree requested the two swim programs share the pool.

Pamela Conley Ulich discussed the public comments heard tonight and consensus
from the community. She requested the City get a generator for City Hall so it
could be used as a community center during power outages. She encouraged young
women to the audience to run for local office in the future.

Josh Spiegel deferred time to Kevin Keegan.

Kevin Keegan discussed the September 23, 2024 City Council meeting and
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of December 9, 2024
  Page 7 of 10

  direction to bring back report on school resource officers. He requested the Council
7W7  schedule an item on school resource officer resources. He discussed Malibu
  Schools AI Study Committee and requested local businesses collaborate with the
  Committee on a report for the City. He discussed an individual experiencing
  homelessness sitting in her car near schools during school hours and requested
  additional parking regulations near the schools.

  Steve Hotchkiss requested the two swim programs share the pool. He discussed
  Malibu Marlin’s current use of the pool and requested allowing 5—6 swimmers per
  lane to increase the capacity of the pool.

  Olea Brinkmann deferred time to Robert Brinkman.

  Robert Brinkman congratulated Councilmember Silverstein, Councilmember
  Uhring and Councilmember Conrad. He stated he was available for questions about
  the Malibu Marlins swim program. He discussed divisions between the swim
  groups and the formation of the Malibu Marlins.

  Kim Sichta congratulated Councilmember Silverstein, Councilmember Uhring and
  Councilmember Conrad. He requested the swim programs share the pool.

  Bill Becker requested shared pool time for the swim programs.

  Bill Sampson congratulated Councilmember Silverstein, Councilmember Uhring
  and Councilmember Conrad. He discussed PSPS events and Southern California
  Edison (SCE). He expressed concern that the beach stairs maintained by the
  MRCA were unsafe. He indicated support for kids swimming and discussed
  accomplished swimmers and water polo players from Malibu.

  Howard Rudzki thanked Councilmember Grisanti for his services.

  Bradley Jessup discussed an open code enforcement case on Councilmember
  Uhring’s property. He discussed John Mazza’s recent comments at a Planning
  Commission meeting that an appeal had already been drafted for an item the
  Commission was considering.

  Steve B. discussed requests to require zoom speakers to appear on video at public
  meetings.  He discussed Councilmember Silverstein’s newly elected
  Councilmember comments and who he choose to thank. He questioned if Jo
  Drummond lived in Malibu when her home was listed on Airbnb.

  Karin Al-Hardan announced the Malibu Education Foundation (MEF) tree lot was
  J  open and that there would special events through the holiday season. She
v,“  congratulated Councilmember Silverstein, Councilmember Uhring and
  Councilmember Conrad on their election.

  Andy Lyon stated he was on generator power during the PSPS event.  He
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of December 9, 2024
  Page 8 of 10

  congratulated Councilmember Silverstein, Councilmember Uhring and
  Councilmember Conrad. He thanked those who voted for him as a write—in
  candidate. He requested the City use backup generators if signal lights went out.
  He discussed LAZ parking enforcement and the number of tickets issued for no
  front license plate.

  ITEM 4.B.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, Community Services Director Riesgo
  discussed the RFQ process in 2024 to select a swim program. She stated the
  contract had a three-year term. She stated staff worked with the Malibu Marlins
  President to determine which programs will be offered, and anyone can join the
  program. She stated the Malibu Marlins offered a competitive program.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins stated she attended the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified
  School District (SMMUSD) Parent-Teachers Association (PTA) breakfast. She
  stated she attended a Clean Power Alliance (CPA) board meeting. She discussed
  US Senate Bill HR5863 allowing tax relief for wildfire victim settlements and
  encouraged the public to request the President sign the bill. She stated front license
  plates are required by the State of California. She stated the LAZ Parking group
  helped address illegal parkers creating public safety hazards. She announced the
  Harry Barovsky Memorial Youth Commission and the Malibu Navy League were
  each holding toy drives for the holidays. She congratulated Councilmember
  Silverstein, Councilmember Uhring and Councilmember Conrad.

  Councilmember Conrad congratulated Councilmember Silverstein and
  Councilmember Uhring, and thanked Councilmember Grisanti for his service. She
  commended Channing Frykman and Andy Lyon on their campaigns. She discussed
  the importance of youth sports, preparing for PSPS events, and school safety.

  Councilmember Uhring discussed the need to address PSPS events. He discussed
  stated items would be coming back on short-term rentals, hybrid meetings and SCE.
  He discussed the potential uses ofAI in schools and a CNN article on the topic. He
  recommended finding compromise between the swim programs.

  Councilmember Silverstein suggested exploring legal recourses for PSPS. He
  discussed short—term rentals and the City’s existing zoning codes. He stated short—
  term rentals were currently prohibited in residential zones. He discussed his
  proposal to limit zoom participation to Malibu residents and requiring speakers to
  sign up in advance. He stated City Hall should be available to the public during
  power outages. He discussed the prohibition on camping in a certain distance from
  schools. He discussed the swim programs and public comment regarding the clubs
  over the last year. He stated he had requested the proposals from the RFQ be
  brought to the Council before the agreement was awarded. He stated everyone who
_.J  wanted to swim should be able to use the pool.

  In response to Mayor Stewart, Assistant City Manager Toney stated in the case of
   Malibu City Council

  fire or an imminent evacuation, generators would be deployed at signal lights
  during PSPS events.

  Mayor Stewart stated the pool should be open to the community and indicated the
  swim groups should work together and with the Parks and Recreation Commission.
  He discussed how the license plate readers will be used as a force multiplier. He
  stated he attended the SMMUSD PTA breakfast with Mayor Pro Tem Riggins. He
  stated he attended a District Metro Board meeting to appoint the Westside District
  Representative on the Metro Board of Directors. He discussed PSPS impacts on
  communication systems during disasters. He discussed the regional impact of
  PSPS events and suggested a regional solution.

  Councilmember Silverstein discussed traffic signals and the declaration of local
  emergency for PCH safety. He indicated support for using generators for signal
  power during all PSPS events.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Riggins, Assistant City Manager Toney stated the
  signal generators were reserved for evacuation purposes. Public Works Director
  DuBoux stated Caltrans indicated they had battery backup for signals, but it was
  unknown if it would last duration of the PSPS event. He stated crews were on
  standby for generator deployment.

  Mayor Pro Tem Riggins stated generators were deployed during the last PSPS
  event.

  In response to Councilmember Uhring, Public Works Director DuBouX stated there
  was an agreement between the City and Caltrans to allow the City to deploy
  generators at Caltrans signals on PCH.

  Councilmember Silverstein requested consensus to bring back an item on PSPS.

CONENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item on Public Safety
  Power Shutoffs and the use of signal generators.

ITEM 5  ORDINANCES AND PUBLIC HEARINGS

  None.

ITEM 6  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 7  NEW BUSINESS

  None.
